claim: Let \(\mathcal T\) be a critical Poisson\((1)\) Galton–Watson tree and define its combinatorial-Laplacian spectral measure by \(\sigma_1(B)=\mathbb E[|V(\mathcal T)|^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf 1_B(\Delta_{\mathcal T})]\). There are constants \(c,E_0>0\) such that \(\sigma_1((0,E])\ge cE^{3/2}\) for every \(0<E<E_0\). Consequently, for no \(c_0>0\) can \(\sigma_1((0,E])\le \exp(-c_0E^{-1/2})\) hold for all sufficiently small \(E\).

integrity.provenance: Mathematical derivation with cited public literature; no independent certification claimed.

scientific_limitations: Proves only a polynomial lower bound; no matching upper bound or exact asymptotic is claimed.
The constants are existential and depend on the conditioned-tree height-limit event.
The claim is about the critical tree-law spectral measure and does not settle the finite-graph zero-atom convergence issue.
title: Polynomial spectral-edge mass for the critical Poisson Galton–Watson tree
